written.myAnswer: Low-molecular-mass covalent substances have weak intermolecular forces, so little energy is needed to separate their molecules. They are therefore often gases or low-boiling liquids.
Carbon, for example as diamond or graphite, is a crystalline solid with covalent bonds between its atoms.
HF molecules form strong hydrogen bonds with one another, so HF is a liquid at room temperature. HCl molecules have weaker intermolecular forces, so HCl is a gas.
Water is polar, while many covalent compounds are non-polar and have little attraction to water molecules. They therefore generally do not dissolve in water.
A white precipitate of silver bromide forms: NaBr(aq) + AgNO₃(aq) → AgBr(s) + NaNO₃(aq).
I₂ molecules have stronger intermolecular forces than Cl₂ molecules, so more energy is needed to separate them. Iodine is solid while chlorine is a gas at room temperature.

Ionic compounds are usually crystalline, brittle solids with high melting points. They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, and are generally soluble in water. Covalent compounds generally have lower melting and boiling points, do not conduct electricity, and are often soluble in organic solvents. Some covalent substances with large molecules are solids.
Graphite conducts electricity because it has mobile electrons that can move through its layers and carry charge.
